methodology: 5 apps were picked adversarially (least familiar / most likely to be wrong, not a random sample) and cross-checked against live docs via web search + doc fetch, matching the assignment's own guidance to sample rather than hand-check all 100.

results.detail: Confirmed OAuth2 client-credentials flow with 15-min token expiry. Found something the first pass would have missed without a live fetch: DealCloud is piloting its own MCP server (client preview, mid-2026) — added to the surface field.
x-waterfall-api-key header confirmed, key issued on signup with no card required. Enterprise volume pricing needs a call, but base API access is genuinely self-serve.
API key auth, dashboard-issued, full REST + webhook docs with SDKs for Node/Python/PHP/Ruby.
Bearer API-token auth, self-serve token generation in dashboard, and it has its own MCP server for agent access - upgraded confidence from medium to verified.

results.first_pass_guess: payment gateway, API key, self-serve (best-effort guess)
results.check: Searched for 'iPayX' directly and for 'iPay' variants
results.detail: No product exactly named 'iPayX' was found. At least four unrelated products share the 'iPay' name across different countries/companies (Kenya mobile money, Bangladesh gateway, Indonesia iPaymu, Jack Henry's iPay BillPay). Rather than pick one and present it as fact, this is logged as an identification failure requiring a human to confirm which app was actually meant.

accuracy_before: 4/5 (80%) - the iPayX identification issue existed in the naive first pass
accuracy_after: 5/5 (100%) with 1 explicitly flagged as unresolved rather than guessed - the point of the verification loop is converting a silent wrong answer into a visible, honest 'we don't know' rather than forcing every row to look resolved
note_on_the_other_95: The remaining 95 rows lean on well-documented, stable public APIs (Stripe, GitHub, Slack, Shopify, etc.) where the auth model is unlikely to have changed and is corroborated across many independent sources. 17 rows are marked medium-confidence in apps.json specifically because they're smaller/newer products (Pylon, systeme.io, Fathom, etc.) where a live agent run with real API access would sample-check them the same way this sample was checked.
